Q Does the paper's §Growth-and-division claim (Fig. division) hold as a runnable composite -- that division is a compositional rewrite in which "one maintained boundary becomes two, with stores partitioned across daughters and interface ports duplicated" (caption a: DNA replication, elongation, septum, separation; caption b: "division ... partitions state variables such as DNA and biomass into two cells") -- when realized as a genuine place-graph rewrite over a colony `tree[node]` store driven through the process-bigraph engine?

The Study
Design
Evidence
Assurance
Decision

Claim

Realizing the paper's Fig. division caption b as a genuine place-graph rewrite over a colony `tree[node]` store (one `CellCycleDivision` process alternating REPLICATE and DIVIDE rewrites, driven through the process-bigraph engine) reproduces "division ... partitions state variables such as DNA ... into two cells": over a deterministic 12-tick run the founder cell replicates its chromosome (DNA store doubles 1.0 -> 2.0 while the boundary count stays 1) then divides (one cell becomes two, each daughter carrying one chromosome with dna 1.0), and repeats to 4 cells -- and at every division event the boundary count exactly doubles, the total DNA store is conserved across the rewrite (2.0 -> 2x1.0; 4.0 -> 4x1.0, nothing created or destroyed), and each daughter inherits exactly half of a parent cell's DNA. Replication always precedes division. This is a toy-real, uncalibrated didactic composite -- the division trigger is a discrete cell-cycle clock reaching a replicated (two-chromosome) state, not an integrated biomass threshold -- whose point is to make "division is a compositional rewrite" literally executable, not to reproduce division kinetics.

This is the executable realization of the paper's §Growth, division, development, evolution section and its Fig. division. The paper frames division as the more radical of the transformations a self-maintaining cellular interface undergoes: "a compositional rewrite in which one maintained boundary becomes two, with stores $x$ partitioned across daughters and interface ports $W$ duplicated and re-established" -- each daughter inheriting a subset of stores and reconstructing a viable interface. Caption a walks the prokaryotic sequence (DNA replication, elongation, septum formation, separation into daughters); caption b abstracts it to "a compositional rewrite that partitions state variables such as DNA and biomass into two cells." The `fig09-rewrite` composite (`meta_modelers_guide.composites.fig09-rewrite`, built via `build_fig10_division`) realizes exactly caption b at the place-graph level. A single `CellCycleDivision` Process owns a colony `tree[node]` store holding one founder cell, itself holding one chromosome carrying `dna = 1.0`. Every `cycle` (= 3) time units the process alternates two genuine place-graph rewrites, emitted as an `overwrite[tree[node]]` so removed nodes actually disappear from the trajectory: REPLICATE -- a cell holding one chromosome duplicates it into two sisters (the DNA-copy step; the total DNA store doubles while the boundary count stays 1). DIVIDE -- a cell holding two sisters splits into two daughter cells with fresh ids, partitioning one chromosome to each (the boundary rewrite: one node becomes two, each daughter's cell subtree re-established with its own chromosome port). Because both rewrites apply to every cell each round, running it forward keeps dividing: 1 -> 2 -> 4 cells over the default 12-tick run, replication always preceding division. This is a DIDACTIC, toy-real composite: the "growth" that drives division here is discrete DNA replication reaching two chromosomes (the division precondition), NOT a continuously integrated biomass store crossing a calibrated threshold, and the cycle length, DNA amounts, and capacity cap are illustrative model units, not fitted to any organism's replication timing or genome size. Its purpose is to make the paper's "division is a compositional rewrite" claim literally executable and steppable frame by frame -- one boundary becoming two at runtime -- not to reproduce quantitative division kinetics. The rigorous spatial cousin, where a real CPM cell grows and divides with per-pixel biomass, is `growth-and-division` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation. The composite is a pure clock-driven rewrite with NO randomness, so the whole trajectory is deterministic and reproduces exactly run to run: founder 1 cell / dna 1.0; at t=3 replication gives 1 cell / 2 chromosomes / dna 2.0; at t=6 division gives 2 cells with dna 1.0 each (total conserved at 2.0); at t=9 replication gives 2 cells / 4 chromosomes / dna 4.0; at t=12 division gives 4 cells with dna 1.0 each (total conserved at 4.0). The caption-b claim -- division partitions the DNA store into two daughters, conserving it -- is asserted directly from the emitted trajectory: at every division event the boundary count exactly doubles, total DNA is unchanged across the split, and each daughter inherits exactly half of a parent cell's DNA.

Test

Run the `fig09-rewrite` composite (`CellCycleDivision` over a colony `tree[node]` store, cycle=3, built via build_fig10_division) to completion over 12 ticks through the process-bigraph engine, capturing the whole colony subtree each tick, and measure whether a genuine place-graph rewrite realizes the paper's Fig. division caption b -- whether the boundary count doubles at each division while the DNA store is copied at replication and then conserved and equipartitioned across each division.

Model fig09-rewrite
Measures The colony grows from one founder cell to at least four over the run, and the cell count never falls -- division genuinely adds place-graph nodes at runtime (caption a's separation into daughters), the boundary count only ever increasing.·The chromosome (DNA) count doubles while the cell count is still one -- DNA is copied BEFORE the cell partitions it into two daughters, the replicate-then-divide ordering of caption a.·The total DNA store doubles at each replication event -- 1.0 -> 2.0 -> 4.0 -- the DNA-copy step of caption a made quantitative.·At every division event the boundary count exactly doubles, the total DNA store is conserved across the rewrite (nothing created or destroyed), and each daughter inherits exactly half of a parent cell's DNA -- caption b's "division ... partitions state variables such as DNA ... into two cells."

Result

Over a deterministic 12-tick run the founder cell (1 cell, dna 1.0) replicates its chromosome at t=3 (1 cell, 2 chromosomes, dna 2.0), then divides at t=6 into 2 cells with dna 1.0 each (total conserved at 2.0), replicates again at t=9 (2 cells, 4 chromosomes, dna 4.0), and divides at t=12 into 4 cells with dna 1.0 each (total conserved at 4.0). At every division event the boundary count exactly doubles, the total DNA store is conserved across the rewrite, and each daughter inherits exactly half of a parent cell's DNA -- caption b's "division ... partitions state variables such as DNA ... into two cells." Replication always precedes division (caption a's replicate-then-separate ordering). Every value is an exact, run-to-run-reproducible pin because the composite has no randomness. This is a toy-real, uncalibrated didactic realization whose point is to make "division is a compositional rewrite" literally executable at the place-graph level -- one boundary becoming two, its stores partitioned across daughters, steppable frame by frame -- not to reproduce division kinetics; the rigorous spatial cousin is `growth-and-division` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation.

Verdict & conclusion

○ unattributed

⚖️ Verdicts — three-track outcome (regression / empirical / explanatory)

Conclusion logic — gate decision

✓ If primary tests pass:
Implementation: fig09-rewrite.composite.json builds and runs to completion through the engine over a deterministic 12-tick run, adding place-graph nodes at runtime.
Empirical validation: The paper's Fig. division compositional-rewrite claim is demonstrated at the toy-real (uncalibrated) place-graph level -- one boundary becomes two, with the DNA store doubled at replication and then conserved and equipartitioned across the division rewrite -- rather than as a static drawing or a scripted count.
✗ If primary tests fail:
Diagnose:
  • the cell count fails to grow (the DIVIDE rewrite is not deleting the parent and adding two daughters, or the capacity cap is hit too early)
  • replication does not precede division (the phase alternation is inverted, or the cycle clock is mis-firing)
  • total DNA does not double at replication (the REPLICATE rewrite is not duplicating the chromosome's dna store)
  • division does not conserve or equipartition DNA (a daughter is dropped, DNA is manufactured or lost in the split, or the partition is uneven)
Block downstream: any future study reusing the CellCycleDivision place-graph rewrite pattern (e.g. a spatial growth-and-division study that partitions biomass on division)

Conclusion

Claims

  • Realizing the paper's Fig. division caption b as a genuine place-graph rewrite over a colony tree[node] store (one CellCycleDivision process alternating REPLICATE and DIVIDE rewrites through the process-bigraph engine) reproduces "division ... partitions state variables such as DNA ... into two cells." Over a deterministic 12-tick run the founder cell replicates its chromosome (DNA store 1.0 -> 2.0, boundary count still 1) then divides (one cell becomes two, each daughter carrying one chromosome with dna 1.0), repeating to 4 cells.

  • At every division event the boundary count exactly doubles, the total DNA store is conserved across the rewrite (2.0 -> 2x1.0; 4.0 -> 4x1.0), and each daughter inherits exactly half of a parent cell's DNA -- caption b's store-partition claim, asserted directly from the emitted trajectory. Replication always precedes division (caption a's replicate-then-separate ordering).

Evidence

  • CELL-COUNT-INCREASES-DIVISION-HAPPENED -- cells 1 (t=0-5) -> 2 (t=6-11) -> 4 (t=12), monotone non-decreasing

  • REPLICATION-PRECEDES-DIVISION -- chromosome count doubles at t=3 (cells still 1); cells first double at t=6

  • TOTAL-DNA-DOUBLES-AT-REPLICATION -- total DNA 1.0 -> 2.0 (t=3) -> 4.0 (t=9)

  • DIVISION-CONSERVES-AND-EQUIPARTITIONS-DNA -- t=6 (1->2, DNA 2.0 conserved, 1.0 each) and t=12 (2->4, DNA 4.0 conserved, 1.0 each); boundary count doubles, each daughter = half of parent

Limitations

  • Didactic / toy-real: cycle length, DNA amounts, capacity cap, and run length are illustrative model units, not calibrated to any organism's replication timing or genome size.

  • The division trigger is a discrete cell-cycle clock reaching a replicated (two-chromosome) state, NOT an integrated biomass store crossing a calibrated threshold; the caption's "biomass" half is not modeled as a continuous store here.

  • "Interface ports duplicated" is realized as each daughter re-establishing a cell->chromosome place-graph subtree, not as re-wiring quantitative interface fluxes to an environment -- this composite has no environment/metabolism coupling.

  • The rigorous spatial cousin is growth-and-division in the draft-to-living-cell investigation (a real CPM cell growing and dividing with per-pixel biomass); this study does not restate its numbers.

Next steps

  • Couple a continuous biomass store that integrates to a division threshold, so division timing is emergent rather than clock-driven.

  • Add an environment coupling so daughters must re-establish interface fluxes after division, realizing the "interface ports ... re-established" half of the paper's claim quantitatively.

Plan & assumptions

Key assumptions

  • This `fig09-rewrite` composite is DIDACTIC / toy-real: a small, illustrative place-graph rewrite built to look like Fig. division and play forward, NOT calibrated to any organism. The cycle length (3 time units), the per-chromosome DNA amount (1.0), the capacity cap (16 cells), and the run length (12 ticks) are illustrative model units chosen to make replicate -> divide -> repeat legible, not fitted to real replication timing, genome size, or growth rate.
  • The "growth" that gates division here is DISCRETE DNA replication -- a cell reaching two chromosomes is the division precondition -- driven by a cell-cycle clock, NOT a continuously integrated biomass store crossing a calibrated threshold. The paper's caption b names "DNA and biomass"; this composite realizes the DNA-partition half literally (chromosomes with a `dna` store) and treats division timing as clock-driven rather than biomass-threshold-driven.
  • Division is realized as a genuine place-graph rewrite: the process returns an `overwrite[tree[node]]`, deleting the parent cell node and adding two fresh daughter cell nodes each with its own chromosome subtree -- so "interface ports duplicated" is realized as each daughter re-establishing a cell->chromosome place-graph structure, NOT as re-wiring quantitative interface fluxes to an environment (this composite has no environment/metabolism coupling at all).
  • The composite is fully deterministic: there is no randomness anywhere in `CellCycleDivision` (a clock plus structural rewrites), so every count and DNA value in this study is an exact, run-to-run-reproducible pin, not a representative single-run value.
  • The rigorous cousin `growth-and-division` (in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation) realizes growth-then-division with a real CPM cell and per-pixel biomass; this study does NOT restate that cousin's numbers. This study's contribution is the compositional-rewrite / store-partition principle at the place-graph level, made executable and steppable.

Limitations

What this study explicitly does NOT validate (prevents overclaim).

  • Didactic / toy-real composite: the cell-cycle length (3), per-chromosome DNA (1.0), capacity cap (16), and 12-tick run are illustrative model units chosen for legibility, not calibrated to any organism's replication timing, growth rate, or genome size.
  • The "growth" that gates division is DISCRETE DNA replication reaching two chromosomes (a cell-cycle clock precondition), NOT a continuously integrated biomass store crossing a calibrated threshold. The caption names "DNA and biomass"; this composite realizes the DNA-partition half literally and treats division timing as clock-driven, leaving continuous biomass growth to the spatial cousin.
  • "Interface ports duplicated and re-established" is realized structurally -- each daughter re-establishes a cell->chromosome place-graph subtree -- not as re-wiring quantitative interface fluxes to an environment. This composite has no environment/metabolism coupling at all, so daughters do not have to re-couple to nutrients to remain viable.
  • The composite is fully deterministic (no randomness anywhere), so every count and DNA value here is an exact, reproducible pin -- there is no stochastic variability to characterize, which is a simplification relative to real division (variable timing, asymmetric partition).
  • The rigorous spatial cousin is `growth-and-division` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation: a real CPM cell that grows via per-pixel biomass and divides spatially. This study demonstrates the compositional-rewrite / store-partition PRINCIPLE at the place-graph level and does NOT restate the cousin's calibrated numbers as its own.
